object_description: high compact volume with a symmetrical shade roof and split-level base
design_condition: The high, compact volume is placed centrally and parallel to the surrounding high-rise blocks, preserving the existing flowing outdoor space while remaining autonomous from the primary school complex.

positive.statement: The high structure allows a small footprint and preserves the flowing outdoor space.

position.target: high structure and flowing outdoor space
position.rationale: Compact footprint and substantial height are evident, with open-space implications around the sampled building mass.

positive.statement: The structural order gives the design its quality.

position.rationale: Regular repeated point rows and horizontal plates visibly establish the building-wide structural order.

positive.statement: The two central staircases create well-proportioned access halls as anterooms to the classrooms.

position.rationale: Interior staircases are not distinguishable; the central access-hall location is approximated at the south-facing surface.

positive.statement: The slope of the terrain is cleverly used to illuminate the gymnasium and create ground-floor zoning.

position.rationale: Split-level lower geometry supports a constrained ground-floor anchor, though the gymnasium itself is interior.

positive.statement: The division of the canteens according to age groups makes sense.

position.rationale: Separate canteens are unrepresented internally; a lower-level zone is estimated on the south-east building surface.

positive.statement: The concrete support plate structure allows great flexibility.

position.rationale: Repeated horizontal support plates are clearly visible across the elevations and anchor the structural system.

positive.statement: The architectural expression with structurally modern themes is convincing in the context of the surrounding buildings.

position.rationale: The tall solitary volume and symmetric roof support an expression anchor; surrounding buildings are not sampled.

negative.statement: The large asphalted break area and all-weather area create a strong contrast to the flowing green space.

position.target: large asphalted break area and all-weather area
position.rationale: Hard-surface areas are absent from the point cloud; the adjacent south-east ground edge provides a constrained estimate.

negative.statement: The poorly designed surroundings and large hard-surface areas do not use the urban-development potential sufficiently.

position.target: poor surroundings and large hard-surface areas
position.rationale: External surroundings are not modeled, so the north-west perimeter is used as a distributed site approximation.

negative.statement: The shade roof limits the quality of stay.

position.rationale: Symmetrical roof geometry is clearly visible at the upper boundary and across the elevation views.

negative.statement: The excavation required to illuminate the gymnasium may seem forced.

position.rationale: Lower split-level geometry suggests excavation at the ground interface, while the gymnasium remains interior.

negative.statement: The kitchen cannot be optimally arranged for both canteens, and meal distribution is constrained.

position.rationale: Kitchen operations are not visible; a lower south-east service zone is used as a constrained anchor.

negative.statement: Views over the district and vertical spatial relationships between floors would make the climb easier.

position.target: views over district and vertical floor relationships
position.rationale: Vertical stacking is visible, but district views are absent; the upper north-east edge approximates the circulation concern.

negative.statement: Individual group rooms and offices are too narrow.

position.rationale: Interior rooms are not distinguishable; a distributed upper-level north-east surface location is estimated.

negative.statement: The basement workshops have only indirect lighting and are unlikely to be eligible for approval.

position.rationale: Basement workshops are interior and unrepresented; the lower south-west surface provides a constrained placement.

negative.statement: Access to the basement floors, workshops and cloakrooms is too small and not sufficiently generous.

position.rationale: Internal access spaces are not identifiable; the lower central south edge approximates the basement circulation zone.

negative.statement: The height, solitary urban setting and architectural expression were questioned for the expanded school complex.

position.target: height, solitary urban setting and architectural expression
position.rationale: Height, compact solitary massing, and roof expression are visible, though the expanded urban complex is absent.
